Key migration patterns you can extract from apq8016_sbc (and reuse for Qualcomm ASoC upstreaming) are:

- DT-first machine description
  - Move board wiring (DAI endpoints, routing, widgets, GPIOs/clocks) to Device Tree.
  - Keep C machine driver thin: parse DT card name/routing and register.

- Generic ASoC link model (not vendor-private)
  - Use standard snd_soc_card + snd_soc_dai_link.
  - Model Front-End/Back-End (DPCM) links explicitly:
    - FE: dynamic PCM endpoints (user-visible streams)
    - BE: no_pcm links to physical interfaces/codecs

- Modern dai_link component definitions
  - Prefer component arrays/macros (CPU/CODEC/PLATFORM components) over legacy string-only fields.
  - Enables cleaner multi-component and future-proof conversion.

- Split codec paths cleanly
  - Represent Qualcomm codec stacks as separate digital/analog paths where applicable.
  - Keep board-specific init (jack, micbias, sysclk) in link init callbacks, not global hacks.

- DAPM-centric power/routing
  - Define widgets/routes for speakers, mics, headphone, etc.
  - Avoid hardcoded power sequencing in platform code; let DAPM drive it.

- Minimal probe + devm lifecycle
  - In probe: parse DT, set up links/routes, register card with devm_snd_soc_register_card.
  - Avoid complex manual cleanup paths.

- Clocking done through ASoC ops
  - Configure MCLK/BCLK/sysclk in hw_params/startup callbacks via standard DAI ops.
  - Remove downstream-style global clock pokes.

- Reuse Qualcomm common helpers
  - Centralize repeated parsing/quirk logic in qcom sound common helpers.
  - Keep machine files board-focused and small.

- Upstream style cleanup from downstream CAF patterns
  - Drop proprietary controls, magic IDs, and static routing tables in code.
  - Replace with bindings + generic controls + standard DAPM/UCM expectations.

- Binding-first upstream strategy
  - Land DT bindings and compatible strings early.
  - Then machine driver + codec/LPASS integration with bisectable FE/BE increments.

Key migration patterns from apq8096-class Qualcomm ASoC machine drivers (useful for upstreaming) are:

1) Board logic moves from C code to Device Tree
- Early machine drivers hardcode dai_links, routing, GPIOs, and jack behavior.
- Upstream direction is DT-driven card description (links, routing, widgets, aux-devs), with machine code only for glue.

2) Monolithic machine driver splits into reusable pieces
- Platform/SoC plumbing (LPASS, Q6 AFE/ASM, clocks) is separated from board/card specifics.
- Common Qualcomm helpers are reused across SoCs instead of duplicating per-board code.

3) FE/BE DPCM model becomes the norm
- Front-end PCM devices are exposed to userspace.
- Back-end links (MI2S/SLIMbus/etc.) are kept internal and routed through DSP/AFE.
- This matches Qualcomm DSP-centric pipelines and scales to new codecs/interfaces.

4) Hardcoded codec assumptions are removed
- Codec model, bus instance, and routing are discovered via DT phandles.
- Same machine logic can work with variant codecs or board revisions.

5) Power/clock handling migrates to runtime PM-friendly flow
- Startup/shutdown hooks only enable what a link needs.
- Clocks/regulators are no longer globally forced on at probe time.
- DAPM routes/widgets are used to represent real power dependencies.

6) Vendor-specific controls are trimmed to upstream-safe controls
- Downstream-only mixer controls and calibration hooks are dropped or abstracted.
- Standard ALSA controls, DAPM, and existing q6* interfaces are preferred.

7) Optional paths are modeled as optional links/components
- APQ vs MSM differences, external amps, or secondary interfaces are represented as optional DT nodes/links.
- Avoid separate near-duplicate machine drivers for small BOM differences.

8) Bindings-first upstreaming sequence
- Define/clean YAML bindings first.
- Then land minimal playback path.
- Add capture, jack-detect, DMIC, voice/offload incrementally.
- This reduces review friction and regression risk.

9) Audio routing is declared, not scripted
- Use snd_soc_of_parse_audio_routing-style DT routing instead of custom C route tables where possible.
- Keeps card topology reviewable and maintainable.

10) Keep machine driver “thin”
- Upstream-preferred Qualcomm machine drivers are mostly:
  probe + parse DT + register card + small fixups.
- Any large policy/state machine logic is a red flag for upstream acceptance.

Key migration patterns seen when moving msm8996-era Qualcomm ASoC audio to upstream:

3) Proprietary MSM audio glue -> standard ASoC DPCM model
- Keep Front-End/Back-End separation, but use standard dynamic PCM flow and upstream q6* interfaces.
- Remove private policy/control paths where possible.

4) Custom mixer/routing controls -> DAPM-centric routing
- Convert hand-managed path enable/disable logic into DAPM widgets/routes.
- Prefer standard ALSA controls over vendor-specific userspace expectations.

5) Platform clock/power sequencing in machine code -> runtime PM in leaf drivers
- Push regulator/clock sequencing into codec/platform drivers.
- Use runtime PM/autosuspend and proper DAPM bias transitions instead of always-on behavior.

6) Codec ecosystem cleanup
- Downstream combos (e.g., Tasha/WCD93xx + external speaker amps) are upstreamed as separate codec drivers and linked via DT.
- Keep machine layer as integrator, not owner of codec internals.

7) Naming/API modernization
- Replace legacy msm_* private APIs with upstream ASoC/Q6 APIs.
- Normalize stream/link naming to reduce userspace fragility and ease UCM migration.

8) Incremental bring-up strategy
- Upstream first with playback/capture on primary path.
- Then add voice use-cases, external amps, jack detect, low-power/offload paths in follow-up patches.

9) Smaller, reviewable patchsets
- Sequence typically: DT bindings -> codec/platform support -> machine driver -> board DTS enablement -> UCM.
- Each step independently testable.

10) Compatibility pattern for old userspace
- Expect control/path name drift versus Android downstream trees.
- Provide UCM2 profiles and avoid kernel-side compatibility hacks unless strictly needed.

Key migration patterns seen from SDM845 ASoC machine work, and reused across Qualcomm audio upstreaming:

2) FE/BE DPCM topology instead of monolithic PCM paths
- Use Qualcomm DSP front-ends (MultiMedia/Voice/etc.) and physical back-ends (MI2S/SLIMbus/DisplayPort) as separate links.
- Makes routing extensible per product without rewriting core machine logic.

3) Reuse of qcom common helpers
- Centralize repeated logic (OF parsing, jack setup, aux devices, card init) into common Qualcomm ASoC code.
- New SoCs/boards add small per-variant tables instead of full custom drivers.

- Keep machine driver generic while external codecs/amps (WCD9xxx, speaker amps, HDMI/DP codec) are separate components.
- Additions become “new endpoint + dai link” rather than invasive machine changes.

- SDM845-era paths rely heavily on SLIMbus/MI2S; newer upstream work moves similar concepts to SoundWire where hardware changed.
- Pattern: preserve ASoC graph semantics while swapping bus/endpoint binding in DT + BE links.

6) DAPM-centric power sequencing
- Replace ad-hoc power toggles with DAPM widgets/routes/events and runtime PM.
- Reduces suspend/resume and pop/click regressions during upstreaming.

7) Incremental upstreaming strategy
- Land minimal playback/capture first, then add jack detection, speaker protection, voice paths, low-power modes, and corner-case routes.
- Keeps reviewable patch series and stable intermediate states.

8) Variant scaling by compatible + data tables
- One machine code path supports multiple products through compatible strings and per-board link/routing tables.
- Avoids copy-paste machine drivers for each device SKU.

  - Replace ad-hoc clock control with runtime PM + standard ASoC startup/hw_params/shutdown sequencing.

  - Use pinctrl states and ASoC jack APIs; avoid vendor-private headset logic in machine code.

- Audio map is expressed in DAPM with standard widgets/routes.

9) Always-on behavior to low-power-safe operation

10) Downstream feature dump to incremental upstream slices

- New SoC bring-up usually becomes: clone variant + adjust offsets/counts/compatibles.

10) Upstream quality pattern

- Demonstrate no regression on existing LPASS variants.
